title: Idempotent config apply + webhook adapter for Optimize cost recommendations (API & SDK)
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Ship a safe, idempotent config-apply API surface and corresponding SDK helpers to let Optimize automation safely enact batching and caching recommendations. Provide a webhook adapter for delivery of recommendation lifecycle events with verification and retry semantics. This ticket implements server-side idempotency, dry-run + preview flow, and SDK ergonomics to reduce operator errors during automated cost ops.
acceptance_criteria: POST /v1/optimize/apply accepts an idempotency_key and returns 202 + operation id if accepted
Repeated POST with same idempotency_key and identical payload returns the same operation id and does not re-run apply
API supports dry_run=true which returns a simulated plan (token estimate, expected latency delta, config diff) without changing runtime state
Webhook endpoint and event schema documented: recommendation.created | recommendation.preview | apply.started | apply.succeeded | apply.failed
Webhook payloads are HMAC-signed; SDK verifies signatures and exposes a helper to validate headers
Server-side safety checks prevent apply if incompatible features detected (e.g., model variant mismatch); response includes a human-readable reason and remediation steps
SDKs for Python/TypeScript expose optimize.applyRecommendation(...) with idempotencyKey, dryRun and waitForCompletion options
E2E tests cover idempotency, edge case of partial failures, and rollback flow triggered by apply.failed
Monitoring/alerting added: metric optimize.apply.latency, optimize.apply.errors (tagged by failure_reason)
implementation_notes: API: new endpoint POST /v1/optimize/apply - request schema includes recommendation_id, target_scope (route/model), idempotency_key, dry_run (bool), apply_options (batch_size, cache_ttl_override)
Server: persist idempotency records in DynamoDB table 'optimize_apply_idempotency' with TTL and request fingerprint
Locking: optimistic apply + compare-and-swap on config revision to avoid stomping concurrent manual changes. If revision mismatch, return 409 with current revision and preview diff
Preview: dry_run invokes planner to produce a Plan object: estimate_tokens_saved, expected_rps change, conflict_warnings[] and a unified diff of config changes
Execute: apply runs as async job (operation_id) on orchestrator; orchestration emits apply.started then apply.succeeded/apply.failed to webhook and console
Rollback: each apply creates a reversible snapshot and stores reversal steps; automatic rollback triggers on majority-failure or explicit apply.failed from safety checks
Webhook adapter: events signed with HMAC-SHA256 using shared secret per-app; include 'X-Optimize-Signature' and timestamp to mitigate replay
SDK ergonomics: TypeScript helper optimize.applyRecommendation({id, idempotencyKey, dryRun, wait}) returns an Operation object with poll() and cancel() helpers
Backwards compatibility: keep legacy URL /v1/recommendations/execute as facade returning redirect to new operation endpoint for 90 days
Rate limiting: apply endpoints throttle to 10/sec per-org to avoid runaway automation; evaluate raising limit for Dedicated customers in follow-up

links: Security ticket: SEC-492 webhook secret rotation
qa_plan: Unit tests for idempotency store: repeated inserts return same op id and do not double-run
Integration: deploy to staging, run harness that fires identical apply requests concurrently and assert single execution
Fault injection: force orchestrator worker crash mid-apply and assert automatic rollback snapshot is applied
Webhook verification: send signed + unsigned events to a test receiver and assert SDK verifies signatures and rejects mismatches
Dry-run validation: compare planner dry-run token estimate with a small-scale shadow run to ensure estimates within 10%
rollback_plan: All applies create an immutable snapshot before mutation. If a catastrophic failure is detected (apply.failed with rollback_recommended) orchestrator will automatically run the snapshot reversal. Manual rollback: console exposes 'revert optimize apply' button which triggers the stored reversal steps; if reversal fails, escalate to on-call infra with runbook 'optimize-apply-revert'.
notes_on_backward_compatibility: Legacy callers that POST to /v1/recommendations/execute will be redirected (307) to /v1/optimize/apply for 90 days. They must start sending idempotency_key to get idempotent semantics.
SDK v1 behavior preserved: old optimize.executeRecommendation() retained but deprecated; logs include deprecation warning for 30 days
Webhook signature header name changed from 'X-Signature' to 'X-Optimize-Signature'; SDK supports both for a transition window and logs mismatch warnings
open_questions: Should we enforce idempotency_key length/format? Current draft allows 64-byte opaque string; security suggested base64url to avoid header encoding issues
What should be the default retention for idempotency records for Dedicated customers with long-lived automation (proposed: 90 days behind a tenant-level flag)?
Edge case: apply with dry_run=false but waitForCompletion=true - how long should server hold http connection? Current plan: 60s timeout and return 202 + polling URL if exceeded
Do we version the webhook event schema (v1) now or defer until follow-ups? Recommended: include event_version in payload to enable future changes
